function.name: get_boiling_melting_points
function.description: Retrieve the boiling point and melting point of a substance based on its name and the sea level. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

message.reasoning:
The user wants boiling point and melting point of water at sea level 5000 meters? Actually "海平面下5000米處" means at altitude 5000 meters below sea level? Wait "海平面下5000米處" could mean at 5000 meters below sea level (i.e., undersea depth). But typical phrase "海拔5000米" would be above sea level. However "海平面下5000米處" literally means "5000 meters below sea level". So they want boiling point and melting point of water at 5000 meters below sea level. That is deep ocean. Pressure increases with depth. At 5000 m depth, pressure ~ 50 atm (~5 MPa). Boiling point increases with pressure. Melting point also changes slightly.

We need to call function get_boiling_melting_points with substance "water" and sea_level 5000? But function expects sea_level in meters. It says "Retrieve the boiling point and melting point of a substance based on its name and the sea level." So we pass sea_level=5000. But the function likely interprets sea_level as altitude relative to sea level. If negative values represent below sea level? The function might handle negative sea_level. We can pass sea_level=-5000? But the user said "海平面下5000米處" meaning below sea level. So we should pass sea_level=-5000. But the function signature expects sea_level: number. So we can pass -5000. Let's do that.

We'll call function get_boiling_melting_points with substance="water", sea_level=-5000.
